big_idea: We use a balance for MASS. We pour for CAPACITY.
learning_intention: We are learning to compare and order by mass and capacity.
student_learning_goal: I can compare and order objects by mass and capacity.
success_criteria: I can use a balance for MASS.
I can ORDER 4 objects by each attribute.
lesson_specific_materials: OPTIONAL: Roo and Cal — if available; otherwise teacher voices both characters in two distinct voices, or substitutes two stuffed animals / paper-bag puppets / pictures on the anchor poster. Activity is unaffected.

minds_on.hook: Roo: I'll BALANCE these 4 objects to find the heaviest. Then I'll POUR to find the cup that holds the most!
minds_on.teacher_script:
Bring children to the carpet. Roo and Cal puppets. 'Friends — yesterday length and area. Today MASS and CAPACITY.'

Review vocabulary. 'Mass = how heavy. Capacity = how much it holds.'

Demo mass. Hold up 4 objects (book, pencil, eraser, scissors). 'Use the balance — heavier side goes DOWN.' Compare pairs. Order: lightest to heaviest.

Demo capacity. Hold up 4 cups of varied size. 'Pour beans from one to the other. Overflow = first cup holds MORE.' Compare. Order: smallest to largest.

More examples:
- 4 balls (different weights) → balance to find heaviest
- 4 containers → pour to find biggest capacity

'Roo says — balance for mass. Pour for capacity.'

'Today we ORDER 4 objects by each.'

steps.instruction: Whole group: order 4 objects by mass, 4 cups by capacity.
Three stations. Station A: Mass Order — balance and order 5 objects. Station B: Capacity Order — pour and order 5 cups. Station C: Mixed — pair compares any 4 objects by mass OR capacity.
Stretch challenge at Station C: order 6 objects.

steps.teacher_prompt: Stop at each pair. Mark the tracker.

differentiation.for_emerging: Stay at Station A. Just mass.
differentiation.for_ell_or_iep: Sentence frame: 'The ___ is heavier than the ___.'
differentiation.for_movement_learners: Children act as a 'living balance' — arms out, lean toward heavier.

formative_check.what_to_look_for: Three signals: uses balance correctly; pours carefully; orders 4+ objects.

discussion_prompts: What does it mean to ORDER 4?
Which was easier — mass or capacity?
consolidation.exit_routine: Each child writes ONE comparison: 'My ___ is heavier than my ___.'

assessment_in_this_lesson.rationale: Lesson 3 captures E2.2 mastery for mass and capacity.

expanded_walkthrough.title: When the child orders by APPEARANCE not by BALANCE — repairing the eyeball-mass trap at Grade 1
expanded_walkthrough.rationale:
The most common Grade-1 trap on E2.2 mass is the eyeball-mass trap: the child looks at 4 objects and orders by visual size, not by actual weight. They miss that mass requires the BALANCE.

This matters because mass and size are different attributes.

The walkthrough covers when a child orders without testing.
expanded_walkthrough.setup: Pair is at Station A. Child has 4 objects: cotton ball, marble, eraser, paper clip. Orders by visible size (cotton ball heaviest because biggest).
expanded_walkthrough.teacher_script:
Crouch. 'You said cotton ball is heaviest because it's biggest. But Roo says — TEST IT on the balance.'

Guide. Place cotton ball on one side, marble on other. Marble side drops. 'See — marble is HEAVIER than cotton ball.'

Generalise. 'Roo says — bigger isn't always heavier. Balance to find out.'

If still using sight: provide surprise pairs. 'Test these.' Force balance use.

Long-term recovery: every mass comparison balances first.

worksheet_brief.purpose: Independent practice of E2.2 mass and capacity.

parts_outline.task: Order 4 objects from lightest (1) to heaviest (4).
Order 4 cups from smallest (1) to largest (4) capacity.
Pick 3 objects in your kitchen. Order by mass OR capacity.
